rag.name: MeasureTheory.integral_smul_eq_self
rag.content:
@[to_additive] -- Porting note: was `@[simp]`
theorem integral_smul_eq_self {μ : Measure α} [SMulInvariantMeasure G α μ] (f : α → E) {g : G} :
    (∫ x, f (g • x) ∂μ) = ∫ x, f x ∂μ := by
  have h : MeasurableEmbedding fun x : α => g • x := (MeasurableEquiv.smul g).measurableEmbedding
  rw [← h.integral_map, map_smul]

informal_statement: For any measure μ on a set A, any group element g in G, and any set s in A, the measure of s under the action of g is equal to the measure of the symmetric action of g on s using the original measure μ.
informal_proof:
First, consider the measure μ and a group element g acting on the measurable space A. The action g • μ represents the measure μ transformed by the group element g. Similarly, the symmetric action (DomMulAct.mk.symm g) • s represents the set s acted upon by the symmetric (or inverse) element of g.

The lemma asserts that applying g to the measure μ and then measuring the set s yields the same result as first applying the symmetric action of g to the set s and then measuring it with the original measure μ. This equality is established by leveraging the properties of measurable equivalences and the preimage operations.

By applying the measurable equivalence smul and using the map_apply function, we can show that both sides of the equation produce the same measure. Specifically, using the preimage_smul_inv function ensures that the symmetric action of g correctly translates the set s into the appropriate form for comparison with the transformed measure. Thus, the lemma holds by these foundational properties of group actions on measures.

id.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.domSMul_apply
id.content:
lemma domSMul_apply (μ : Measure A) (g : Gᵈᵐᵃ) (s : Set A) :
    (g • μ) s = μ ((DomMulAct.mk.symm g) • s) := by
  refine ((MeasurableEquiv.smul ((DomMulAct.mk.symm g : G)⁻¹)).map_apply _).trans ?_
  congr 1
  exact Set.preimage_smul_inv (DomMulAct.mk.symm g) s

C1_dependencies.name: MeasurableEquiv.smul
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- If a group `G` acts on `α` by measurable maps, then each element `c : G` defines a measurable
automorphism of `α`. -/
@[to_additive (attr := simps! (config := .asFn) toEquiv apply)
      "If an additive group `G` acts on `α` by measurable maps, then each element `c : G`
      defines a measurable automorphism of `α`." ]
def smul (c : G) : α ≃ᵐ α where
  toEquiv := MulAction.toPerm c
  measurable_toFun := measurable_const_smul c
  measurable_invFun := measurable_const_smul c⁻¹

C1_dependencies.content:
/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
